en: Wading through the long years' steeping
Crossing through how many arrayed dynasties
Having weathered a thousand years of wind, rain, frost and cold

zh: 石板街面拓印歲月蒼桑
彫欄簷角懸垂藝術光輝
胡同窄巷述說古老故事
鐘樓寺院掩映前賢智慧
en: The stone-paved street imprints the vicissitudes of time
Carved railings and eaves hang with artistic splendor
The narrow hutong alleys tell ancient stories
Bell tower and temple half-hide the wisdom of the sages before us
Wars no more, the horses' neighing long faded
City walls built up from knife scars and gunfire
Still surveying the four directions with stern dignity
White walls and red tiles packed close, scale upon scale
Still leisurely mirroring the blue sky
And the sea-foam of the Adriatic
Still gently, unhurriedly rolling and unfurling against the shore
As the sea wind turns cool
Looking back
This bears witness to history
A castle of singular style
Still within the dusk that comes to meet it
Reflecting on times past
Reshaping memory

points.zh: 亞德里亞海有數的小島和半島，在夏日陽光的照映下，閃耀迷人。曲折的海岸散落著許多村落和古城，之中要數位於克羅埃西亞南端的杜布魯夫尼克最亮麗，最富城堡韻味，詩人拜倫遊歷後，稱此古城是亞德里亞海灘上遺落的珍珠。1979年列入聯合國世界文化遺產。這個建立於6世紀的古老城市，有著令人眼花撩亮的歷史典故，人文起落。斑斑史冊延拓千年，拜占庭帝國統領過，威尼斯大公國佔屬過，奧匈帝國入侵過，奧圖曼帝國控管過。就在最近的20多年前，南斯拉夫崩潰後的戰亂， 1991~1992年間，遭受鄰國塞爾維亞的南斯拉夫人民軍團的猛烈攻擊，歷時9個月，在斷水斷電，彈盡援絕之下，憑藉城民自組的剛毅力量，竟得成功的保住老城。老城被高大厚實的城牆團團圍住，圍住了滄桑歷史，建築藝術和人文風情。登臨城牆，環繞遊走石板石階，不但城內城外風光盡收眼底，遼濶的亞德里亞海和點點風帆，也令人心神飄盪。而紅瓦，白牆，藍天，碧波，遠近錯落，竟是極色彩之美。
points.en: The Adriatic Sea's numerous small islands and peninsulas shimmer beautifully under the summer sun. Along the winding coastline are scattered many villages and ancient towns, among which Dubrovnik, at the southern tip of Croatia, is the most dazzling and richly evocative of castle romance. After traveling there, the poet Byron called this ancient city "the pearl dropped on the Adriatic shore." It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. Founded in the 6th century, this ancient city has a dazzling array of historical episodes and cultural ups and downs. Its annals span a thousand years: ruled at various times by the Byzantine Empire, held by the Republic of Venice, invaded by the Austro-Hungarian Empire, and controlled by the Ottoman Empire. Just over twenty years ago, amid the chaos following the collapse of Yugoslavia, between 1991 and 1992, the city suffered fierce attacks from the Yugoslav People's Army of neighboring Serbia, lasting nine months. Cut off from water and electricity, and with supplies and reinforcements exhausted, the old town was nonetheless successfully preserved through the resolute strength of its self-organized citizens. The old town is surrounded by tall, thick walls that enclose its layered history, architectural art, and cultural atmosphere. Climbing onto the walls and walking along the stone paving and steps, one can take in the scenery both inside and outside the town, while the vast Adriatic Sea dotted with sails also stirs the spirit. The red tiles, white walls, blue sky, and turquoise waves, arranged near and far, form a scene of extraordinary color.
